 Falcon 9 SpaceX launches classified payload for the U.S. Space Force
 Will Robinson-Smith November 19, 2026 
 11:51 p.m. 
 SpaceX's Falcon 9 rocket stands at Space Launch Complex 4 East at Vandenberg Space Force Base ahead of the launch of the USSF-317 mission. Image: SpaceX
 Update Nov. 20, 11:45 p.m. EDT (0445 UTC): SpaceX landed its booster on the  drone ship. 
 SpaceX launched an undisclosed number of satellites on a Falcon 9 rocket on behalf of the U.S. Space Force on Friday night. SpaceX scrubbed the launch Thursday night, but didn’t state the reason why.
 The mission, designated USSF-317, flew from Space Launch Complex 4 East at Vandenberg Space Force Base at 8:20 p.m. PST / 11:20 p.m. EST (0420 UTC on Saturday, Nov. 21). The rocket took off on a south-easterly trajectory upon leaving the pad.
 Plays from YouTube 
 This is the latest in a series of ‘R’ missions assigned to SpaceX. So far, there have been five previous such missions which include:
 Aug. 16 – USSF-366 (R-1)
 Sep. 10 – USSF-153 (R-2)
 Sep. 26 – USSF-385 (R-3)
 Nov. 06 – USSF-432 (R-4)
 Nov. 12 – USSF-627 (R-5)
 Following each of these launches, 23 satellites have been catalogued. To date, the U.S. Space Force hasn’t confirmed details about these satellites and has not made statements following these launches to confirm successful deployments.
 SpaceX launched the USSF-317 mission using the Falcon 9 first stage booster with the tail number B1100. This was its 11th flight following the launches a NROL-105-, USSF-385, and eight batches of Starlink satellites.
 A little more than eight minutes after liftoff, B1100 landed on the droneship, Of Course I Still Love You . This was the 235th landing on this vessel and the 679th Falcon booster landing to date.
 SpaceX is scheduled to launch at least two more missions for the U.S. Space Force before the end of the month.
